compound_or_probe_identity: Reagent pair: (a) clemastine or benztropine, two M1 antagonist chemotypes also inhibiting EBP; (b) a structurally unrelated EBP inhibitor without M1 affinity (TASIN-1, or the CW9956/CW9009/CW3388 family: identity from the held ledger rows, in vitro only); (c) genetic control: Chrm1-null versus wild-type OPCs. No compound is nominated for use ADDED after V13: (d) PIPE-307, an M1-selective antagonist (V13 read: Ki about 4.6 nM at M1, more than ten-fold over M2-M5, 47-target panel clean at 10 uM; EC50 38.6 nM in primary rat OPCs; raises a myelination index in a primary rat cortical neuron-OPC assay; EBP activity untested; PMID 39083422, read by V13 at partial_fulltext_read, not by this producer); a clean muscarinic arm, not yet a clean non-sterol arm. M3-selective antagonist inactive
pharmacology_sources: Hubler 2018 PMID 30046109 and Allimuthu 2019 PMID 30773481 (sterol/EBP, OPC monoculture, held ledger partial reads, not re-read); Mei 2016 Chrm1 knockouts (held summary R14-R18, primary not opened); Bohlen 2023 PMID 37068912 (clemastine, read this run); Ettle 2016 PMID 27059609 (abstract)
role: probe pair (reagent pair that separates two readings of one drug) with clemastine as the reusable drug comparator
known_in_neuron_driven_model: Not shown for a neuron-driven defect. Intrinsic-defect models only: Tcf4 het (EM g-ratio and uncompacted share, CAP N1/N2 ratio), Pdk1 icKO (marker, synapse, behaviour), alpha-synuclein (abstract). Tcf4 het total myelinated-axon density was NOT restored
transferred_from_injury_or_wild_type: wild-type neonatal mouse: markers up, callosal conduction velocity down (held E39-E40); adult lysolecithin and cuprizone acceleration (Deshmukh/Mei, held); neostigmine opposite (R52)
counter_evidence: (1) Chrm1-null OPCs differentiate about five-fold more and the drug effect is lost only there (held R14-R16) versus EBP inhibition, not M1 blockade, predicts the effect (held R33): unreconciled in held material. (2) Wild-type neonatal conduction fell. (3) Total myelinated axon density not restored in Tcf4 het (V01). (4) Uninjured myelin unchanged by OPC Chrm1 deletion (R17) (V13) acetylcholine inhibits OPC differentiation (IC50 about 58 nM; about 12 nM in OPC-conditioned medium): an antagonist needs tone, so the inert antimuscarinics in Hubler may reflect missing tone (INFERENZA, untested)
comparator_for_functional_outcome: sheath structure in the dish (MBP+ internodes per axon length and internode length, with a marker level beside it); conduction not measurable in the dish: next level is a slice or callosal CAP arm, and for a wild-type neuron condition the adverse-effect arm
control_that_separates_mechanism: NOT INTERPRETABLE AS WRITTEN: clemastine/benztropine in Chrm1-null OPCs cannot separate routes because the null baseline already equals the drug effect (about five-fold), so loss of the drug effect is expected under either route. Replacement contrasts (V13): (i) an EBP inhibitor without M1 affinity in Chrm1-null OPCs; (ii) PIPE-307 with and without an EBP inhibitor (additive or not, Hubler additivity logic); (iii) EBP loss with PIPE-307; plus M1 expression and acetylcholine tone in the OPC preparation; sterol profile as engagement
two_chemotypes_same_target_shown: two chemotypes on one target: shown for EBP in OPC monoculture (clemastine, benztropine, tamoxifen, U50488 and independent scaffolds) by held ledger rows; NOT shown to be the only route for clemastine because the Chrm1 genetic result disagrees. Not assumed
marker_reflects_function_shown: not shown. Hubler: MBP+ formation and microfibre ensheathment in vitro; Tcf4 het: marker and EM and CAP all moved in the same direction (intrinsic defect); wild-type neonatal: marker and conduction diverged
adult_injury_label_and_transfer: Mixed: adult-injury evidence (lysolecithin, cuprizone, hypoxia) for most compounds; the transfer to development is not established (neonatal clemastine impaired conduction in wild type) and is stated as such

compound_or_probe_identity: Lipid and substrate supply arm: cholesterol and fatty-acid enrichment (diet-level in vivo evidence only) and ketone bodies as axonal substrate. Dish reagents (cholesterol carrier, fatty-acid mix, beta-hydroxybutyrate) are NOT verified in any source read for this co-culture
pharmacology_sources: Camargo 2017 PMID 28549068 (read this run: astrocyte-SCAP, HFD from E15, conduction); Dietary KD Plp1tgB PMID 30919030 (read this run); SLC44A1 citicoline abstract PMID 41317319; aspartoacylase abstract PMID 27717881 (genetic)
role: proposal without an interpretable reagent in the dish (the in vivo diet result is a control for the supply explanation; the dish reagent must first be shown to enter myelin membrane there)
known_in_neuron_driven_model: Not tested with a neuron-driven defect. Defect outside the oligodendrocyte but in the astrocyte: HFD rescued myelination (text) and callosal fast-wave presence (5 to 50 percent of slices). KD: conduction gain exceeded myelination gain in an oligodendrocyte-intrinsic model
transferred_from_injury_or_wild_type: oligodendrocyte-intrinsic models (PLP overexpression, SLC44A1, ASPA) and cuprizone remyelination (KD)
counter_evidence: Cholesterol with an intact barrier gave no major benefit in two PMD patients and little in the BBB-intact mouse; HFD rescue is partial; exposure began at E15 (prevention), and a delay in lipid synthesis can normalise by itself with age (CNP-SCAP P20 to P120) (V13) in the CNP-SCAP/GFAP-SCAP double mutant a high-fat diet gave no improvement and animals died at P15-P21; mct8 zebrafish: T3 rescue only before BBB maturation
comparator_for_functional_outcome: callosal or optic nerve CAP and EM g-ratio on diet versus control; in the dish, internode number and length with the supply arm in both neuron genotypes
control_that_separates_mechanism: a wild-type neuron condition and a vehicle carrier control; tracer lipid (plant sterol or labelled cholesterol) in myelin as engagement (shown in vivo: campesterol/sitosterol in myelin)
two_chemotypes_same_target_shown: not applicable to chemotypes; cholesterol versus ketone bodies act on different aspects (the KD paper: cholesterol did not reverse axonal mitochondrial enlargement, KD did)
marker_reflects_function_shown: not shown: CAP gain exceeded myelination gain in KD; oligodendrocyte counts were normal with thin myelin in the astrocyte model
adult_injury_label_and_transfer: Developmental in vivo diets; adult cuprizone arm only for KD. Transfer to neuron-driven hypomyelination not established

compound_or_probe_identity: REVISED after V13 (2026-11-13): reagent pair with PIPE-307 (M1-selective) and an EBP inhibitor without M1 affinity (TASIN-1 or the CW9956 family; the identity and M1 affinity of the EBP inhibitor rest on held ledger rows and an abstract (PMID 38470227), re-verified from no primary paper by either reader; PIPE-307's own EBP activity is untested; the PIPE-307 assay is a primary rat cortical myelination assay (MBP/Tuj1), its neuron-OPC composition an inference); clemastine as the comparator; no compound nominated for use
pharmacology_sources: V13-read: PMID 39083422, Mei 2016 (PMID 27671734), Hubler, Allimuthu; ledger-held rows; producer-read Tcf4 paper
role: probe pair; PIPE-307 is the clean M1 arm
transferred_from_injury_or_wild_type: adult injury (EAE VEP latency and g-ratio with PIPE-307, per V13), wild type, global-allele Tcf4
counter_evidence: M1 route needs acetylcholine tone (IC50 about 58 nM for ACh); Chrm1-null baseline occludes; neonatal clemastine slowed conduction and the authors attribute effects to microglia, absent in the dish
comparator_for_functional_outcome: MBP/Tuj1 segment-length index in a cortical neuron-OPC assay (PIPE-307 paper format) and, in the DRG co-culture, internode scoring or EM beside the MBP morphology classes
control_that_separates_mechanism: additivity contrast (PIPE-307 plus EBP inhibitor, additive or not); EBP inhibitor in Chrm1-null OPCs; M1 expression and ACh tone; dose-response with a monoculture ceiling; T3 co-arm; PIPE-307 sterol profile and an assay-window gate (the drug must act on its own before an interaction is read); submaximal doses in a dose matrix (Hubler's non-additivity was at a maximal ketoconazole dose, n >= 3 wells) with a T3 headroom control; contrasts in Chrm1-null or EBP-null cells are read only when positive (the null baselines occlude); rat versus mouse OPC stated
two_chemotypes_same_target_shown: EBP: shown for several chemotypes in EpiSC OPC monoculture; M1: PIPE-307 and MT7 act in primary OPCs; the two are not shown to be one target
marker_reflects_function_shown: not shown (Tcf4 all levels same way; neonatal wild type diverged)
adult_injury_label_and_transfer: Adult injury and wild-type evidence mostly; transfer to development unstated

compound_or_probe_identity: NEURONAL-SIGNAL LEVER (new, after V13): neuron-derived inhibitory signal (CTGF-type, candidate for Wwox-null neurons NOT identified) and neuron mTOR; perturbations: rapamycin or RAD001 in neuron-specific Tsc1 models (reference), conditioned medium from wild-type versus Wwox-null neurons on OPC monoculture, neutralisation of a candidate (CTGF-neutralising antibody in Ercan); no compound nominated for use
pharmacology_sources: Ercan 2017 PMID 28183733 (V13, queried_not_full_read); Meikle 2008 PMID 18495876 (abstract; held R50); J4 PMID 42310739 (mixed context)
role: probe (conditioned-medium assay with a neutralisation control); rapamycin/RAD001 as neuron-side reference perturbations only
known_in_neuron_driven_model: Neuronal Tsc1/Tsc2 models: rapamycin P7-P21 reversed MBP and CC1 deficits (marker); the authors report that neuron-secreted CTGF is necessary and sufficient to block OPC maturation in vitro (the authors' claim, read at targeted depth; Methods and n unread); neuronal CTGF loss restores percent myelinated axons but not g-ratio; no conduction readout; no Wwox datum
counter_evidence: count versus thickness split: a neuron-side fix of the block does not restore sheath thickness (Ercan); early-window treatment only (R50); Wwox null neurons are not shown to release any inhibitory factor (the held note found no conditioned-medium arm)
comparator_for_functional_outcome: conditioned-medium effect on MBP+ share in OPC monoculture, then internode or EM in a co-culture
control_that_separates_mechanism: wild-type neuron medium and a positive control medium (Tsc2-knockdown neuron medium, per Ercan) and neutralisation of the candidate; medium cell-count and viability matched; positive control: recombinant CTGF and HEK-derived CTGF medium (Ercan reports both reduce MBP+ cells) in addition to Tsc2-knockdown neuron medium; fresh-medium baseline, a mixing arm (null medium with wild-type medium), neuron purity checked, a dilution series, the T3/B27 caveat
marker_reflects_function_shown: marker only in Ercan; sheath thickness not restored
adult_injury_label_and_transfer: Developmental neuron-side models; transfer to Wwox not established
